Drop.text: Remove the top value from the stack.

DropN.text: Remove several values. Put the count on top of the values you want to remove; the count is removed too.

Dup.text: Make a second copy of the top value. Example: 7 DUP leaves 7 and 7.

Dup2.text: Copy the top pair of values, keeping their order.

DupN.text: Copy a group of values. Put the size of the group on top first.

Swap.text: Exchange the top two values. Example: 2 3 SWAP leaves 3 below 2.

Over.text: Copy the second value to the top without removing either original value.

Pick.text: Copy a chosen stack level. Put the level number on top first; level 1 is the value immediately below it.

Rot.text: Rotate the top three values, bringing the deepest of the three to the top.

Roll.text: Bring a chosen stack level to the top, moving the intervening values down. Supply the level number first.

RollD.text: Move the top value down to a chosen level. Supply the destination level number first.

Depth.text: Put the number of stack values on top of the stack.

Purge.text: Remove the variable named on the stack. Use a quoted name to avoid evaluating it first.

Sto.text: Store a value under a name: type 42 'ANSWER' STO and press Enter. To keep HOME variables after restart, save the calculator session.

Rcl.text: Fetch a stored object without running it: type 'ANSWER' RCL. A recalled program stays on the stack until you run EVAL.

Eval.text: Evaluate the top object. For a program, this runs its instructions. Example: « 2 3 + » EVAL gives 5.

LastArg.text: Recall the arguments saved from the previous command. Argument-saving settings determine what is available.

LastX.text: Recall the last saved first argument.

ClearStack.text: Remove every value from the stack. Save anything important before using this command.

Nip.text: Remove the second stack value and keep the top one.

Pick3.text: Copy the third stack value to the top.

UnPick.text: Replace a chosen stack level with the supplied value. Check the level before replacing it.

UnRot.text: Rotate the top three values in the opposite direction to ROT.

NDupN.text: Repeat a group of stack values using the supplied count.

DupDup.text: Duplicate the top value twice, leaving three copies.

Clone.text: Make an independent copy of the top object.

Copy.text: Copy a named object between calculator directories using the supplied source and destination names.

Vars.text: List names in the current calculator directory.

TVars.text: List variables of the requested object type in the current directory.

XVars.text: List variables used by the supplied expression.

LName.text: Find names used in the supplied object.

Path.text: Return the path through calculator variable directories to the current directory.

CurrentDirectory.text: Return the current calculator directory as an object. This is calculator variable storage, not an SD folder.

Home.text: Return to the HOME calculator directory.

CrDir.text: Create a calculator variable directory with the supplied name.

UpDir.text: Move to the parent calculator directory.

PgDir.text: Purge the named calculator directory and its contents.

Order.text: Reorder the current directory using a list of variable names.

Undo.text: Restore the saved calculator stack from before the last operation, when stack saving is enabled.

add.text: Add the top two values. Type 2 3 + and press Enter to get 5.

subtract.text: Subtract the top value from the value below it. Example: 10 3 - gives 7.

multiply.text: Multiply the top two values. Example: 6 7 * gives 42.

divide.text: Divide the second value by the top value. Example: 1 3 / keeps the exact fraction when exact arithmetic is enabled.

mod.text: Find the mathematical modulo of two numbers, in dividend then divisor order. Negative inputs can differ from REM.

rem.text: Find the division remainder, in dividend then divisor order. Example: 5 2 rem gives 1.

pow.text: Raise the second value to the power on top. Example: 2 3 ^ gives 8. On the calculator stack, a complete numeric entry such as 2^3 also gives 8 on Enter. 0^0 gives 1 by default; the advanced ZeroPowerZeroIsUndefined setting explicitly selects undefined behavior.

neg.text: Change the sign of the top value.

abs.text: Find the absolute value, or the magnitude of a complex value.

inv.text: Find the reciprocal of the top value: 1 divided by that value. Zero has no finite reciprocal.

sqrt.text: Find the square root. The real/complex result setting determines whether negative real inputs can give complex results.

sq.text: Square the top value. Example: 12 SQ gives 144.

cubed.text: Cube the top value. Example: 3 cubed gives 27.

ToDecimal.text: Convert the top value to a decimal approximation using the current precision.

ToFraction.text: Convert a value to a fraction using the fraction-conversion settings.

ToQuotient.text: Rewrite a value or expression as a quotient where supported.

cbrt.text: Find the cube root of the top value.

hypot.text: Find sqrt(x^2+y^2) from two supplied values.

xroot.text: Find a root of the supplied value using the supplied root order.

sign.text: Return the sign of a real value, or its normalized direction when supported for complex values.

IntPart.text: Keep the integer part, truncating toward zero.

FracPart.text: Keep the fractional remainder after truncation toward zero.

ceil.text: Round up to the next integer.

floor.text: Round down to the previous integer.

Round.text: Round a value using the supplied digit count. The sign of the digit count selects the engine's rounding convention.

Truncate.text: Discard digits using the supplied digit count instead of rounding them.

mant.text: Return the decimal mantissa of a number.

xpon.text: Return the decimal exponent of a number.

SigDig.text: Count the significant decimal digits of a value.

Percent.text: Calculate a percentage of the value below it. The base amount goes first, then the percentage.

PercentChange.text: Calculate percentage change from the first value to the second.

PercentTotal.text: Calculate the second amount as a percentage of the first total.

Min.text: Keep the smaller of the top two values.

Max.text: Keep the larger of the top two values.

DFC.text: Convert a decimal value to a continued-fraction representation.

DFC2F.text: Convert a continued-fraction representation to a fraction.

Extract.text: Extract the requested part of an object using the supplied selection information.

Pi.text: Put the mathematical constant pi on the stack. Symbolic/numerical constant settings affect its form.

EulerianNumber.text: Put Euler's number e on the stack. Symbolic/numerical constant settings affect its form.

Infinity.text: Put positive infinity on the stack.

NegativeInfinity.text: Put negative infinity on the stack.

RealToBinary.text: Convert a real integer to a based-number object. Base and WordSize control its representation and fixed-width operations.

BinaryToReal.text: Convert a based integer to a real-number object.

Factors.text: Factor an integer, subject to the configured factorization limits.

IsPrime.text: Test whether the supplied integer is prime.

NextPrime.text: Find the next prime after the supplied integer.

PreviousPrime.text: Find the preceding prime before the supplied integer.

GCD.text: Find the greatest common divisor of two integers.

LCM.text: Find the least common multiple of two integers.

Div2.text: Perform integer division and return the quotient and remainder.

RandomSeed.text: Set the random-number generator seed. Reusing a seed is useful when reproducing a calculation.

RandomNumber.text: Generate a random value from 0 up to, but not including, 1.

Random.text: Generate a random value between two supplied bounds. Put the lower bound first and the upper bound on top.

asin.text: Find the inverse sine of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

acos.text: Find the inverse cosine of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

atan.text: Find the inverse tangent of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

sin.text: Find the sine of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

cos.text: Find the cosine of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

tan.text: Find the tangent of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

sec.text: Find the secant of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

csc.text: Find the cosecant of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

cot.text: Find the cotangent of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

asec.text: Find the inverse secant of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

acsc.text: Find the inverse cosecant of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

acot.text: Find the inverse cotangent of the top value. Real angles follow the calculator angle mode; choose Degrees or Radians before calculating.

asinh.text: Calculate the inverse hyperbolic sine for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

acosh.text: Calculate the inverse hyperbolic cosine for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

atanh.text: Calculate the inverse hyperbolic tangent for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

acsch.text: Calculate the inverse hyperbolic cosecant for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

asech.text: Calculate the inverse hyperbolic secant for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

acoth.text: Calculate the inverse hyperbolic cotangent for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

sinh.text: Calculate the hyperbolic sine for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

cosh.text: Calculate the hyperbolic cosine for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

tanh.text: Calculate the hyperbolic tangent for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

csch.text: Calculate the hyperbolic cosecant for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

sech.text: Calculate the hyperbolic secant for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

coth.text: Calculate the hyperbolic cotangent for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

ln.text: Calculate the natural logarithm for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

exp.text: Calculate the exponential e^x for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

log10.text: Calculate the base-ten logarithm for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

exp10.text: Calculate the exponential 10^x for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

ln1p.text: Calculate the natural logarithm of 1+x for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

expm1.text: Calculate the value of e^x-1 for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

log2.text: Calculate the base-two logarithm for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

exp2.text: Calculate the exponential 2^x for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted.

erf.text: Calculate the error function for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted. Complex arguments are not implemented for this function.

erfc.text: Calculate the complementary error function for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted. Complex arguments are not implemented for this function.

tgamma.text: Calculate the gamma function for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted. Complex arguments are not implemented for this function.

lgamma.text: Calculate the logarithm of the gamma function for the top stack value. Its real domain and the real/complex result setting determine which inputs are accepted. Complex arguments are not implemented for this function.

GammaP.text: Calculate the regularized lower incomplete gamma function. Enter a followed by x, with a>0 and x>=0.

BetaI.text: Calculate the regularized incomplete beta function. Enter a, b, then x; a and b must be positive and x must be between 0 and 1.

UTPC.text: Find the upper-tail chi-square probability. Enter degrees of freedom followed by the statistic x. Degrees of freedom must be positive.

UTPN.text: Find the upper-tail normal probability. Enter mean, variance, then x. The variance must be positive; it is variance, not standard deviation.

UTPT.text: Find the upper-tail Student t probability. Enter positive degrees of freedom followed by t.

UTPF.text: Find the upper-tail F probability. Enter numerator degrees of freedom, denominator degrees of freedom, then x. Both degree counts must be positive.

fact.text: Find the factorial. Noninteger arguments follow the engine's gamma-function extension where supported. On the calculator stack, press ! with an empty editor to apply factorial immediately. Typing 6! also calculates immediately, without Enter. Inside programs and quoted algebra, ! remains notation.

Termial.text: Sum the integers from 1 through n. Accepts nonnegative whole numbers, including zero. Uses n*(n+1)/2 and returns an exact integer; negative or fractional inputs report a domain error. Enter 6? or 6 Termial to get 21. With no entry being edited, press ? to apply Termial immediately to the top stack value. Typing 6? also calculates immediately without Enter; inside programs and quoted algebra, ? remains notation. In algebraic expressions, N? is postfix Termial(N). In RPL, use N ? or N Termial after a variable; question marks in ordinary RPL identifiers remain valid. Explicit names such as ⓋREADY? and the constant Ⓒ? keep their existing meanings.

comb.text: Count unordered selections. Supply population size n followed by selection size r.

perm.text: Count ordered selections. Supply population size n followed by selection size r.

True.text: Put a true Boolean value on the stack.

False.text: Put a false Boolean value on the stack.

And.text: Combine two values with AND. Integer inputs follow the truth/bitwise logic setting.

Or.text: Combine two values with OR. Integer inputs follow the truth/bitwise logic setting.

Xor.text: Combine two values with exclusive OR. Integer inputs follow the truth/bitwise logic setting.

Not.text: Invert a truth value or bits, according to the integer logic setting.

same.text: Compare two objects for identical content and type, rather than mathematical equivalence.

TestSame.text: Test whether the supplied objects are the same, using the engine comparison operation.

TestLT.text: Test whether the second stack value is less than the top value.

TestEQ.text: Test whether the top two values are equal.

TestGT.text: Test whether the second stack value is greater than the top value.

TestLE.text: Test whether the second stack value is less than or equal to the top value.

TestNE.text: Test whether the top two values differ.

TestGE.text: Test whether the second stack value is greater than or equal to the top value.

IFTE.text: Choose between two branches from a condition. Supply the condition, true branch and false branch in that order.

IFT.text: Run the supplied branch only when the supplied condition is true.

Where.text: Apply the supplied local assignments to an expression.

NSub.text: Return the current subsequence index while DoSubs is running. Outside that operation there is no such local index.

EndSub.text: Return the final subsequence index while DoSubs is running.

SetFlag.text: Set the numbered user flag supplied on the stack.

ClearFlag.text: Clear the numbered user flag supplied on the stack.

TestFlagSet.text: Test whether the supplied user flag is set.

TestFlagClear.text: Test whether the supplied user flag is clear.

TestFlagClearThenClear.text: Test whether a user flag was clear, then leave it clear.

TestFlagClearThenSet.text: Test whether a user flag was clear, then set it.

TestFlagSetThenClear.text: Test whether a user flag was set, then clear it.

TestFlagSetThenSet.text: Test whether a user flag was set, then leave it set.

FlagsToBinary.text: Pack the engine flag state into a based integer for storage or inspection.

BinaryToFlags.text: Restore engine flag state from a supplied based integer. This can change calculator behavior.

FlipFlag.text: Toggle the numbered user flag supplied on the stack.

Compile.text: Parse source text into calculator objects. It does not run a Lua or CHIP-8 file.

CompileToAlgebraic.text: Parse source text and require an algebraic object.

CompileToNumber.text: Parse source text and require a number.

CompileToInteger.text: Parse source text and require an integer.

CompileToPositive.text: Parse source text and require a positive value.

CompileToReal.text: Parse source text and require a real value.

CompileToObject.text: Parse source text as one calculator object.

CompileToExpression.text: Parse source text and require an expression.

ToProgram.text: Turn the supplied object into an RPL program.

ToInteger.text: Convert a supported object to an integer.

Quote.text: Keep the supplied expression unevaluated in the applicable symbolic context.

Halt.text: Pause RPL execution so you can inspect or debug it.

Debug.text: Start the supplied RPL program in the debugger.

SingleStep.text: Execute the next instruction of a paused RPL program.

StepOver.text: Run the next instruction without stepping into a called program.

StepOut.text: Continue until the current nested program returns.

MultipleSteps.text: Execute the supplied number of debugger steps.

Input.text: Ask for calculator input using the supplied prompt specification.

Prompt.text: Display the supplied prompt during RPL execution.

Run.text: Run the supplied program or named object. In Programming browsers, use the labelled F2 Run action.

TimedEval.text: Evaluate an object and report its elapsed time.

Wait.text: Wait for the supplied duration or a key, according to the engine WAIT convention. Returned key positions are engine keys, not QWERTY character codes.

ToText.text: Convert the top object to its source-text representation.

ToList.text: Collect the requested number of stack values into a list. Supply the count last.

FromList.text: Unpack a list into its elements and return its size using the engine list convention.

Explode.text: Break an object into its components.

Put.text: Replace an element in the supplied object at the supplied position.

Get.text: Read an element from the supplied object at the supplied position.

Size.text: Return an object's size, such as a list length or matrix dimensions.

Sort.text: Sort list elements in ascending order.

QuickSort.text: Sort a list in ascending order with the engine quick-sort operation.

ReverseSort.text: Sort list elements in descending order.

ReverseQuickSort.text: Sort a list in descending order with quick sort.

ReverseList.text: Reverse the order of list elements.

QuickUnique.text: Remove duplicate elements using the engine quick unique operation.

Head.text: Return the first element of a list.

Tail.text: Return the list after removing its first element.

Map.text: Apply the supplied operation to list elements and collect the results.

Reduce.text: Combine list elements using the supplied operation.

Filter.text: Keep list elements that pass the supplied test.

DoList.text: Apply an operation across one or more lists. Supply the lists, their count and the operation using the engine list convention.

DoSubs.text: Apply an operation to list subsequences. NSub and EndSub provide local indices while it runs.

ListSum.text: Add the elements of a list.

ListProduct.text: Multiply the elements of a list.

ListDifferences.text: Return differences between successive list elements.

GetI.text: Read the indexed element and advance the index using the engine indexed-access convention.

PutI.text: Write the indexed element and advance the index using the engine indexed-access convention.

CharToUnicode.text: Return the Unicode code point for a supplied character.

UnicodeToText.text: Build text from supplied Unicode code points.

TextToUnicode.text: Return the Unicode code points in supplied text.

Sum.text: Evaluate a summation from an expression, variable and bounds.

Product.text: Evaluate a product over an expression, variable and bounds.

Root.text: Find a local numerical solution. Supply an expression, quoted variable and initial guess. Example: Rad 16 Precision 'COS(X)-X' 'X' 1 Root gives X near 0.7390851332. Ctrl+W offers the guided solver.

MultipleEquationsSolver.text: Solve several equations numerically using the supplied variables and guesses. Ctrl+W > Equation system is the guided alternative.

MultipleVariablesSolver.text: Solve using the supplied equation, variables and starting values through the engine multi-variable solver.

Integrate.text: Numerically integrate an expression over the supplied variable and bounds. Home > Math & graphs > Calculus provides a guided definite integral.

Subst.text: Substitute the supplied replacement into an expression without assigning a calculator variable.

MatchUp.text: Apply a symbolic rewrite while traversing the expression upward.

MatchDown.text: Apply a symbolic rewrite while traversing the expression downward.

Expand.text: Expand products and powers in an algebraic expression.

Collect.text: Collect matching terms in an algebraic expression.

PartFrac.text: Decompose a rational expression into partial fractions where supported.

FoldConstants.text: Combine the constant parts of an expression.

ReorderTerms.text: Put expression terms into the engine's canonical order.

Simplify.text: Simplify an expression using the current algebra rules.

TrigSin.text: Rewrite trigonometric expressions in terms of sine where supported.

ToPolynomial.text: Convert an expression to the engine polynomial representation.

FromPolynomial.text: Convert a polynomial object back to an algebraic expression.

PEval.text: Evaluate a polynomial using the supplied argument.

PRoot.text: Find roots of the supplied polynomial using the polynomial solver.

PCoef.text: Return polynomial coefficients using the engine's coefficient order.

Zeros.text: Find zeros using the engine symbolic/polynomial operation. A result is subject to the expression and solver limitations.

Apply.text: Apply a supplied symbolic transformation to an expression.

Isolate.text: Rearrange an equation to isolate the supplied variable. Some equations cannot be isolated by the engine.

Derivative.text: Differentiate an expression with respect to a quoted variable. Example: 'X^2' 'X' Derivative gives 2*X.

Primitive.text: Find a symbolic antiderivative. Example: 'X^2' 'X' Primitive gives X^3/3. The arbitrary constant is implicit.

AlgebraConfiguration.text: Return the calculator directory used for algebra configuration.

StoreAlgebraVariable.text: Set the algebra variable from the supplied name.

StEq.text: Store the supplied equation as the engine's current equation.

NextEq.text: Select the next equation in the engine equation set.

Equation.text: Use the supplied equation definition in the engine equation/library context.

re.text: Return the real part of a complex value.

im.text: Return the imaginary part of a complex value.

arg.text: Return the phase of a complex value in the current angle unit. Zero has no defined direction.

dot.text: Calculate the dot product of two vectors.

cross.text: Calculate the cross product of two compatible vectors.

det.text: Find a square matrix's determinant. Example: [[1 2][3 4]] DET gives -2.

norm.text: Find the norm of the supplied vector or matrix.

MatrixToColumns.text: Split a matrix into column vectors.

MatrixToRows.text: Split a matrix into row vectors.

ColumnsToMatrix.text: Build a matrix from supplied column vectors.

RowsToMatrix.text: Build a matrix from supplied row vectors.

AddColumn.text: Insert the supplied column into a matrix at the supplied position.

AddRow.text: Insert the supplied row into a matrix at the supplied position.

DeleteColumn.text: Remove the specified column from a matrix.

DeleteRow.text: Remove the specified row from a matrix.

REF.text: Reduce a matrix to row echelon form.

RREF.text: Reduce a matrix to reduced row echelon form.

RREFP.text: Reduce a matrix and also return its pivot values. The reduced matrix is on top of the stack, with the pivot list below it.

RREFMOD.text: Modulo row reduction is not implemented in this engine build and reports an error. Use REF or RREF for ordinary row reduction.

LU.text: Factor a matrix into lower and upper triangular factors using the engine pivoting convention.

ToArray.text: Build an array from the supplied values and dimensions.

FromArray.text: Unpack an array into its values and dimensions.

ConstantArray.text: Build an array filled with a supplied constant.

IdentityMatrix.text: Build a square identity matrix of the supplied size.

RandomMatrix.text: Build a matrix of random entries with the supplied dimensions.

TransConjugate.text: Transpose a matrix and conjugate its entries.

RealToRectangular.text: Combine two real components into a rectangular complex value.

RealToPolar.text: Combine magnitude and phase into a polar complex value.

RectangularToReal.text: Split a rectangular complex value into real components.

PolarToReal.text: Split a polar complex value into magnitude and phase.

ToRectangular.text: Convert a complex value or coordinate object to rectangular form.

ToPolar.text: Convert a complex value or coordinate object to polar form.

To2DVector.text: Build a two-component vector from supplied values.

To3DVector.text: Build a three-component vector from supplied values.

Convert.text: Convert a quantity to the supplied target unit. Example: 100_cm 1_m Convert gives 1 m. Ctrl+U offers From/To unit lists.

UBase.text: Express a quantity in base units.

UVal.text: Extract the value from a unit-bearing quantity.

UFact.text: Factor a quantity's units using the supplied unit factor.

ToUnit.text: Combine the supplied value and unit into a quantity. Use Convert to change an existing quantity to another unit.

ApplyUnit.text: Attach the unit chosen by the current engine unit-menu key. The menu supplies the unit; typing this helper alone does not choose one.

ConvertToUnit.text: Convert to the unit supplied by the current engine unit-menu key. Ctrl+U is easier for a guided conversion.

ApplyInverseUnit.text: Attach the reciprocal of the unit supplied by the current unit-menu key.

ConvertToUnitPrefix.text: Apply the prefix supplied by the active engine unit-prefix menu key.

UnitsSIPrefixCycle.text: Cycle the SI prefix used by a unit-bearing value.

FromRange.text: Unpack a range into its defining values.

ToRange.text: Build a range from supplied bounds.

ToDeltaRange.text: Build a range using a central value and absolute uncertainty.

ToPercentRange.text: Build a range using a central value and percentage uncertainty.

ToUncertain.text: Build an uncertain number from a central value and standard deviation. Converting an existing range to this representation is not implemented.

RangeUnion.text: Return the union of two ranges where representable.

RangeIntersect.text: Return the overlap of two ranges.

StandardUncertainty.text: Return a quantity's absolute standard uncertainty.

ToStandardUncertainty.text: Build an uncertain quantity using absolute uncertainty.

ToRelativeUncertainty.text: Build an uncertain quantity using relative uncertainty.

StandardRound.text: Round using the supplied absolute uncertainty.

RelativeRound.text: Round using the supplied relative uncertainty.

FromHMS.text: Convert hours/minutes/seconds form to decimal hours.

ToDMS.text: Convert an angle to degrees/minutes/seconds form.

DateAdd.text: Add the supplied number of days to a date.

DateSub.text: Find the difference between supplied dates.

JulianDayNumber.text: Convert a date to its Julian day number.

DateFromJulianDayNumber.text: Convert a Julian day number to a date.

RadiansToDegrees.text: Convert a plain radian value to degrees.

DegreesToRadians.text: Convert a plain degree value to radians.

ToGrads.text: Express an angle in grads: 400 grads make a full turn.

ToPiRadians.text: Express an angle as a multiple of pi radians: 2 makes a full turn.

Date.text: Put the calculator's current date on the stack.

Time.text: Put the calculator's current time on the stack.

DateTime.text: Return the calculator's date and time.

ChronoTime.text: Return calculator time with hundredths of a second in hms form. This reads the clock; it does not connect to NTP.

Ticks.text: Return the engine tick counter for elapsed-time measurements.

SetDate.text: Set the calculator date from the supplied date value. Settings > Clock / timezone offers the native clock options.

SetTime.text: Set the calculator time from the supplied time value. Use actual current time for HTTPS rate updates.

StatsData.text: Access the engine statistical-data object. Ctrl+D uses a separate native data table.

AddData.text: Add supplied observations to the engine statistical data.

RemoveData.text: Remove supplied observations from the engine statistical data.

RecallData.text: Recall the engine statistical-data object onto the stack.

StoreData.text: Replace engine statistical data with the supplied object. Save native Data tables through their CSV file menu.

Average.text: Calculate the mean using the engine statistical data or supplied supported object.

Median.text: Calculate the median of the supplied data.

MinData.text: Return column minima from engine statistical data.

MaxData.text: Return column maxima from engine statistical data.

SumOfX.text: Return the sum of values in the independent data column.

SumOfY.text: Return the sum of values in the dependent data column.

SumOfXY.text: Return the sum of paired X*Y values.

SumOfXSquares.text: Return the sum of squared X values.

SumOfYSquares.text: Return the sum of squared Y values.

Variance.text: Return sample variance from the engine statistical data.

Correlation.text: Return the correlation coefficient for the engine selected data columns.

Covariance.text: Return sample covariance for the engine selected data columns.

StandardDeviation.text: Return sample standard deviation from engine statistical data.

FrequencyBins.text: Count observations in the supplied frequency bins.

PopulationVariance.text: Return population variance, using the full population denominator.

DataTotal.text: Return totals from the engine statistical data.

DataColumns.text: Configure the statistical columns used by engine analysis.

Intercept.text: Recall the intercept last computed by LinearRegression. Run the regression after changing data.

Slope.text: Recall the slope last computed by LinearRegression. Importing data alone does not calculate it.

LinearRegression.text: Fit a linear regression using engine statistical data.

PredictX.text: Predict X from a supplied Y using the current engine regression.

PredictY.text: Predict Y from a supplied X using the current engine regression.

RegressionFormula.text: Return the current engine regression equation. Native Data regression is managed through Ctrl+D.

BestFit.text: Choose the best engine regression fit among its supported models.

LinearFit.text: Select the engine linear regression model.

ExponentialFit.text: Select the engine exponential regression model.

PowerFit.text: Select the engine power-law regression model.

LogarithmicFit.text: Select the engine logarithmic regression model.

TVMAmort.text: Calculate amortization using engine TVM variables.

TVMAmortTable.text: Build an amortization table using engine TVM variables.

TVMRoot.text: Solve the engine time-value-of-money equation for the selected unknown.

TVMEquation.text: Return the time-value-of-money equation. The native Financial calculator keeps its own saved inputs.

StoreAdd.text: Update the named variable using add arithmetic with the supplied value. Supply the value and quoted variable name.

RecallAdd.text: Recall the named value and combine it with a stack value using add arithmetic, without storing the result back.

StoreSub.text: Update the named variable using subtract arithmetic with the supplied value. Supply the value and quoted variable name.

RecallSub.text: Recall the named value and combine it with a stack value using subtract arithmetic, without storing the result back.

StoreMul.text: Update the named variable using multiply arithmetic with the supplied value. Supply the value and quoted variable name.

RecallMul.text: Recall the named value and combine it with a stack value using multiply arithmetic, without storing the result back.

StoreDiv.text: Update the named variable using divide arithmetic with the supplied value. Supply the value and quoted variable name.

RecallDiv.text: Recall the named value and combine it with a stack value using divide arithmetic, without storing the result back.

Increment.text: Increase the supplied value or named variable by one.

Decrement.text: Decrease the supplied value or named variable by one.

RL.text: Rotate the bits of a based integer left within WordSize.

RR.text: Rotate the bits of a based integer right within WordSize.

RLB.text: Rotate a based integer left by one byte.

RRB.text: Rotate a based integer right by one byte.

SL.text: Shift a based integer left, filling vacated bits with zero.

SR.text: Shift a based integer right, filling vacated bits with zero.

SLB.text: Shift a based integer left by one byte.

SRB.text: Shift a based integer right by one byte.

ASR.text: Shift a based integer right while preserving its sign bit.

ASRB.text: Shift a based integer right by one byte while preserving its sign bit.

RLC.text: Rotate a based integer left by the supplied count.

RRC.text: Rotate a based integer right by the supplied count.

SLC.text: Shift a based integer left by the supplied count.

SRC.text: Shift a based integer right by the supplied count.

ASRC.text: Shift a based integer right by the supplied count while preserving its sign.

SetBit.text: Set the requested bit in a based integer.

ClearBit.text: Clear the requested bit in a based integer.

FlipBit.text: Toggle the requested bit in a based integer.

FirstBitSet.text: Find the first set bit using the engine's bit-position convention.

LastBitSet.text: Find the last set bit using the engine's bit-position convention.

CountBits.text: Count the set bits of an integer.

NAnd.text: Return NOT-AND for the supplied operands.

NOr.text: Return NOT-OR for the supplied operands.

Implies.text: Test logical implication from the first operand to the second.

Equiv.text: Test logical equivalence of the supplied operands.

Excludes.text: Test the engine logical exclusion relation for the supplied operands.

RecallWordSize.text: Put the current based-integer word size on the stack.

PlotParameters.text: Read or set the engine plot parameters using the supplied plot-parameter object.

Disp.text: Display supplied text or an object at the requested engine display line.

DispXY.text: Draw supplied text or an object at the requested graphics position.

PixOn.text: Set the pixel at the supplied graphics position using the foreground pattern.

PixOff.text: Clear the pixel at the supplied graphics position using the background pattern.

PixTest.text: Test the pixel at the supplied graphics position.

PixColor.text: Return the colour at the supplied graphics position.

Line.text: Draw between two supplied positions in the engine graphics view.

Ellipse.text: Draw an ellipse using the supplied bounds in the engine graphics view.

Circle.text: Draw a circle using the supplied centre and radius in the engine graphics view.

Rect.text: Draw a rectangle between supplied corners.

RRect.text: Draw a rounded rectangle using supplied bounds and corner radius.

Draw.text: Draw the current engine equation using its plot parameters. For LumaRPL's interactive graph tools, press Ctrl+G.

Drax.text: Draw axes in the engine graphics view using its plot parameters.

ToLCD.text: Copy a graphics object to the calculator graphics display.

FromLCD.text: Capture calculator display pixels as a graphics object.

Function.text: Select function plotting in the engine plot parameters.

Polar.text: Select polar plotting in the engine plot parameters.

Parametric.text: Select parametric plotting in the engine plot parameters.

Truth.text: Select truth plotting in the engine plot parameters.

Scatter.text: Select engine scatter plotting from engine statistical data.

Freeze.text: Set the engine display-region freeze mask. This is a drawing control, not a native graph pause button.

Clip.text: Set the engine graphics clipping region from the supplied object.

CurrentClip.text: Return the current engine graphics clipping region.

Gray.text: Build a greyscale drawing pattern from the supplied intensity.

RGB.text: Build a drawing pattern from red, green and blue components. Foreground and Background accept drawing patterns; themes are selected under Settings > Display.

HSV.text: Build a drawing pattern from hue, saturation and value.

Color.text: Convert the supplied colour specification to an engine drawing pattern.

ToGrob.text: Render the supplied object into a graphics object.

ToHPGrob.text: Convert to an HP-compatible graphics object.

ToBitmap.text: Convert to a packed monochrome bitmap.

BlankGraphic.text: Create a blank graphics object with supplied dimensions.

BlankGrob.text: Create a blank compatibility graphics object with supplied dimensions.

BlankBitmap.text: Create a blank monochrome bitmap with supplied dimensions.

BlankPixmap.text: Create a blank colour pixmap with supplied dimensions.

GXor.text: Combine graphics objects with exclusive OR.

Pict.text: Recall the engine picture graphics object.

GraphicAppend.text: Join graphics objects side by side.

GraphicStack.text: Place graphics objects above one another.

GraphicSubscript.text: Compose a graphics object with a subscript.

GraphicExponent.text: Compose a graphics object with an exponent.

GraphicRatio.text: Compose graphics objects as a fraction.

GraphicRoot.text: Compose a graphics object with a root sign.

GraphicParentheses.text: Surround a graphics object with parentheses.

GraphicNorm.text: Surround a graphics object with norm bars.

GraphicSum.text: Compose graphics objects using summation notation.

GraphicProduct.text: Compose graphics objects using product notation.

GraphicIntegral.text: Compose graphics objects using integral notation.

PlotMin.text: Set the engine plot's minimum corner.

PlotMax.text: Set the engine plot's maximum corner.

XRange.text: Set the engine horizontal plot interval.

YRange.text: Set the engine vertical plot interval.

XScale.text: Set the engine horizontal plot scale.

YScale.text: Set the engine vertical plot scale.

Indep.text: Choose the engine plot's independent variable.

Depnd.text: Choose the engine plot's dependent variable.

Header.text: Set the calculator engine header using the supplied header object.

KeyMap.text: Store a complete engine virtual-key map from the supplied directory object. This is an advanced RPL key-assignment operation, separate from PicoCalc physical shortcuts.

AssignKey.text: Assign an object to an engine virtual-key position.

StandardKey.text: Use the standard engine action for a virtual-key position.

Beep.text: Play a tone. Supply frequency in Hz followed by duration in seconds; for example 440 0.1 Beep. BeepOn enables sound.

Menu.text: Open the supplied engine menu or custom menu definition.

TemporaryMenu.text: Show a temporary engine menu using the supplied definition.

PurgeAll.text: Remove calculator variables in the applicable directory scope. Save important state first.

SystemMemory.text: The original system-memory diagnostic is unavailable here and returns zero. Open Settings > Device status > Memory / PSRAM for PicoCalc memory information.

errm.text: Return the most recent calculator error message.

errn.text: Return the most recent calculator error number.

err0.text: Clear the current calculator error. Esc also dismisses a visible error.

doerr.text: Raise an error from the supplied message or error value.

ToTag.text: Attach the supplied label to an object.

FromTag.text: Remove a tag and return its contents using the engine tag convention.

Cycle.text: Cycle the supplied object between its supported forms.

Type.text: Return the type number of the supplied object.

TypeName.text: Return the type name of the supplied object.

Version.text: Return the engine version information. About LumaRPL shows the installed PicoCalc release.

Bytes.text: Return information about an object’s bytes and its binary check representation.

ScreenCapture.text: The original hardware screenshot command is unavailable on PicoCalc. Use Export from a native graph for SVG or sampled CSV.

KeyEval.text: Evaluate an engine virtual-key action. Its key positions refer to the engine keypad, not physical QWERTY character codes.

KeyCode.text: Return the object assigned to a supplied engine virtual-key position. The position is an engine keypad code, not an ASCII character or physical QWERTY key.

Help.text: Open the LumaRPL command reference. Its lists and pages use the same arrows, Enter and F5/Back controls as the rest of Help.

FlightRecorderConfigure.text: Configure the engine developer flight recorder with the supplied configuration. Recorder output depends on build diagnostics.

FlightRecorderDump.text: Send flight-recorder data to the configured diagnostic output.

FlightRecorderDumpSome.text: Send selected flight-recorder data to diagnostic output using the supplied selection.

Const.text: Look up the supplied name in the constants library. Its SD resource must be available.

ConstantName.text: Return the name of a library constant.

ConstantValue.text: Return the value of a library constant.

ConstantRange.text: Return the range of a library constant when its definition includes uncertainty.

LibEq.text: Load an equation from the equation library using the supplied reference.

XLib.text: Load or call an SD library object using its library reference.

Modes.text: Put a program containing the nondefault calculator settings on the stack. Type EVAL to apply that program. The Advanced RPL settings →Prog key performs this action.

ResetModes.text: Restore the engine's default calculator settings. This changes settings, so save the session first if you want to keep the current ones.

SaveState.text: Save engine calculator state using the supplied state-file workflow. Ctrl+S is the normal PicoCalc session-save shortcut.

BatteryVoltage.text: A measured battery voltage is unavailable on PicoCalc. Use Settings > Device status > Battery for the keyboard controller's percentage and charging state.

PowerVoltage.text: The port cannot provide a measured supply voltage through this command. Use Device status > Battery instead.

USBPowered.text: On PicoCalc this returns True when the keyboard battery controller reports charging, and False otherwise. It is not an independent USB-cable detector. Unknown battery data can also give False; Battery status shows whether a reading is available.

DMCPLowBattery.text: Read the platform low-battery flag supplied by the PicoCalc backend.

LowBattery.text: This legacy voltage-threshold check cannot measure PicoCalc battery health. Use Device status > Battery.

Unimplemented.text: Report that an engine operation has no implementation in this build.

VariablesMenu.text: Open the calculator variable soft menu. Tab selects a row; F1-F5 and Ctrl+F5 choose its columns.

CustomMenu.text: Open the calculator custom soft menu defined by its custom-menu settings.

ToggleCustomMenu.text: Switch the engine custom soft menu on or off.

SolvingMenu.text: Open the engine equation-variable solver menu. Ctrl+W provides guided single-equation and system solving.

FinanceSolverMenu.text: Open the engine TVM-variable solver menu. The native Financial calculator has separate saved inputs.

ToolsMenu.text: Open the context-sensitive calculator soft menu for the current object or entry.

Catalog.text: Open the calculator command catalogue. Ctrl+A opens it directly; choosing an entry inserts its name.

ToggleUserMode.text: Toggle engine user-key mode. This concerns virtual-key assignments, not a new QWERTY alphabet mode.

Off.text: Request engine power-off. To save documents and return to the PicoCalc loader, use Ctrl+Q.

OffWithImage.text: Request engine power-off with its off-image behavior. Ctrl+Q is the safe save-and-return-to-loader workflow.

SystemSetup.text: Open PicoCalc Settings, the same screen as the System action in Advanced RPL settings.

Edit.text: Edit the top stack object in calculator command entry. To edit an SD RPL or Lua file, open it through Programming instead.

StackEditor.text: Open the interactive stack. Arrows select a stack level; Tab chooses the action row; F1-F5 and Ctrl+F5 run the displayed action.

LastMenu.text: Return to the previous calculator soft menu. Pressing Esc now does this directly; at the top level Esc clears the menu.

UILeftShift.text: Select the engine's left-shift command plane for virtual-key automation. For ordinary PicoCalc soft menus, press Tab to select the row you can see.

UIRightShift.text: Select the engine's right-shift command plane for virtual-key automation. Use Tab for everyday menu-row selection; numerical bit shifts are different commands.

UINoShift.text: Select the engine's unshifted command plane. It does not change physical Caps Lock. Tab selects the displayed normal menu row.

UIAlpha.text: Enable uppercase letters on the engine virtual keypad. You can already type letters directly on PicoCalc; use physical Shift/Caps Lock to change their case.

UILowercase.text: Enable lowercase letters on the engine virtual keypad. For normal PicoCalc typing, use physical Shift/Caps Lock.

UINoAlpha.text: Leave the engine virtual keypad's alphabetic mode. Physical QWERTY letters remain available.

UIAlgebraic.text: Invoke the engine algebraic-entry key. Normally type an expression in single quotes, such as 'X^2+1'.

UIExit.text: Invoke the calculator-entry cancel operation. Physical Esc also handles PicoCalc menu Back navigation.

UIDecimal.text: Insert the decimal separator chosen in calculator settings at the calculator-entry cursor.

UIText.text: Invoke the calculator text-entry key. Normally type RPL text inside double quotes, such as "Hello".

UIEnter.text: Submit the current calculator entry through the engine. The physical Enter key is the ordinary way to do this.

UILeft.text: Move left in calculator entry, or open the interactive stack when the entry state calls for it.

UIRight.text: Move right in calculator entry, or begin object editing when the entry state calls for it.

UIUp.text: Move up in calculator entry or recall entry history, depending on the current entry state.

UIDown.text: Move down in calculator entry or open its editor menu, depending on the current entry state.

UIBackspace.text: Delete to the left of the calculator-entry cursor.

UIDelete.text: Delete to the right of the calculator-entry cursor.

EditorSelect.text: Mark a selection anchor in calculator entry. Moving the cursor then changes the selection. In an SD source file, use Ctrl+K to mark text instead.

EditorWordLeft.text: Move the calculator-entry cursor one word left.

EditorWordRight.text: Move the calculator-entry cursor one word right.

EditorBegin.text: Move to the start of calculator entry.

EditorEnd.text: Move to the end of calculator entry.

EditorCut.text: Cut selected calculator-entry text to the calculator clipboard.

EditorCopy.text: Copy selected calculator-entry text to the calculator clipboard.

EditorPaste.text: Insert the calculator clipboard contents into calculator entry.

EditorSearch.text: Start or repeat a search within calculator entry. In an SD source file, use Ctrl+F.

EditorReplace.text: Replace the active calculator search selection with clipboard text and continue searching. An active search, selection and clipboard are needed. For an SD source file, use Ctrl+R.

EditorClear.text: Delete selected calculator-entry text. With no selection, nothing is deleted.

EditorFlip.text: Exchange the calculator selection anchor and cursor so you can extend the other end of the selection.

EditorHistory.text: Recall an entry from calculator command history.

EditorHistoryBack.text: Move through calculator command history in the opposite direction.

atan2.text: Find the angle of a two-component direction using the engine two-argument arctangent; the result follows the current angle mode.

Show.text: Show an enlarged rendering of the supplied calculator object. This is separate from plotting a native saved graph.
